missionPremise: Z1 (P-147) proved live, twice (primary+replica, zero drift), that the 3,376-parcel residual blocking eight rails' gate across five in-scope counties was NOT an unresolved zoningDistrict -- it is legitimate, permanent not-applicable (unzoned land inside a city whose staged zoning layer is declared complete, per src/config/zoning-layer-completeness.mjs). The actual defect: parcel-setback-cells.mjs and parcel-envelope-cells.mjs only ever advanced a parcel's dependent rails when zoningDistrict reached value or refused -- there was no branch for not-applicable, so it was silently lumped in with unaccounted and deferred forever. This is the program's own vacuous-write-path defect class (a code path that runs perfectly and cannot succeed for a population, because no branch exists to move it) pointed at itself.
completionPredicate: unaccounted count for the eight dependent rails (setbackFrontFt/Side/Rear/Corner, setbackRules, maxHeightFt, maxLotCoveragePct, maxFootprintSqFt) on in-city parcels in the five in-scope counties reaches zero, AND the parcel_gate_verdict for each of those 40 (county,rail) pairs flips to pass on the next evaluation. BOTH measured live, independently, after the full apply: (1) a direct query of the completeness-sweep not-applicable population (zoningDistrict cell_state carrying a completenessDeclaration payload) joined against all 8 dependent rails, summed across 5 counties, returns unaccounted=0 -- exact zero, not inferred. (2) A broader sanity check on setbackFrontFt (representative of all 8, since every branch in both writers moves its rails together) shows ZERO 'unaccounted' rows anywhere in the full county-wide population (not just the 3,376 subset) for any of the 5 in-scope counties -- the fix closed the ONLY remaining unaccounted source for these rails, confirming the dispatch's own claim that this population was the entire blocker. (3) parcel_gate_verdict re-evaluated live (targeted trigger of factory-publish-gate-sched covering exactly these 40 pairs, not waiting for the hourly scheduler): all 40 rows now read verdict=pass, unaccounted_count=0, evaluated_at within the trigger's execution window (2026-09-11T13:41-14:10Z). Both predicate halves pass, live, at the cell level and the gate-verdict level.

Out of scope, all confirmed untouched: parcelAreaSqFt (never reads zoningDistrict at all; the new branch lives entirely inside the zoningDistrict-dependent code path, structurally unreachable from parcelAreaSqFt's own loop -- confirmed by an adversarial sub-agent review reading the loop boundaries directly, not merely asserted); zoning-layer-completeness.mjs and parcel-r5-zoning.mjs (read-only inputs to this lane, not edited -- this lane consumes the already-written zoningDistrict not-applicable cell and its completenessDeclaration, it does not change how or when that cell gets written); SETBACK_APPLY_HELD / the atom setback writer (never routed through); Hays 48209 (IN_SCOPE_COUNTIES inherited verbatim by both files, S2 imports it from S1; structurally unreachable, zero rows touched -- confirmed 0 by construction, and Hays's own 570-parcel version of this same population remains untouched and unaccounted, exactly as it should per the P-145 gate); slating / parcelRecordAllowlist.ts's PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE (S5/P-148 and successor own this; this lane only affects parcel_record_cell and, via the existing scheduled gate, parcel_gate_verdict); the stale Elgin '1,680 held' prose figure Z1 flagged (registered separately per the dispatch, not this lane's file to edit).

fleetMemoryScratch.text: When two writers share the same upstream-propagation shape (refused-propagation already existed in both S1 and S2 before this lane), adding a sibling branch (not-applicable-propagation) is safest done by mirroring the existing branch's exact structure (same position in the if-chain, same all-rails-together write, same reuse of the upstream cell's own reason) rather than inventing a new shape -- minimizes the surface an adversarial review has to check from scratch.

A per-parcel counting convention (S1) and a per-cell counting convention (S2) can coexist correctly in two sibling writers for the same logical event -- do not assume a count mismatch across two writers processing the same parcels is a bug before checking each writer's own established counting convention for its OTHER branches (S2's value/refused/absentVerified counts were already per-cell before this lane touched anything).

A kind-based counts switch/if-chain with a catch-all 'else' bucket silently absorbs any new kind you forget to add an explicit branch for -- the write path is unaffected (JSON.stringify preserves the real kind) but the self-reported operational totals lie. Caught this lane's own instance at CP1 adversarial review, before any code ran; worth a standing checklist item whenever a job gains a new disposition kind: grep for every counts-bucketing switch, not just the ones near the new write logic.
